history.headline: The first big trail effort has landed — a long, low-HR day on foot at controlled intensity. This is durability work, not a race pace. The gap between narrative and data has closed.
watch_items: Watch whether the cardio-load status reverses out of its detraining reading once the long effort registers — the speed of that flip is a fair proxy for how hard this day loaded you.
Watch how the day or two after the long effort look: whether easy-run HR sits normal or runs elevated, which will tell you how much the effort actually cost.
Watch whether nightly recovery consolidates now that the logistics-heavy window is passing, since the recent nights are still short and broken.
Watch for any back-to-back long efforts appearing — that's the durability quality this block is genuinely training, and worth confirming in the data.

history.headline: Back-to-back ultra-distance days on foot at controlled HR — the durability quality this block trains, confirmed in the clearest terms yet. The engine held its shape across both. Recovery is now the story.
watch_items: Watch whether the cardio-load status flips out of detraining now that both long days are logged — a slow flip signals a heavier real cost than the low HR implied.
Watch the first few easy runs after the crossing for elevated HR at normal pace, which would show the effort is still being paid down.
Watch whether nightly sleep consolidates now that the crossing window is closing, since recent nights have been short and fragmented.
Watch when strength re-enters the log — its return is a fair marker that the trail block has been absorbed and normal training rhythm has resumed.

history.headline: Three back-to-back ultra days are logged and the trail block is complete. The engine held its shape at controlled HR throughout. The story now is absorption — recovery and the return to normal rhythm.
watch_items: Watch whether the cardio-load status flips out of detraining as the rolling averages catch up to the crossing — a slow flip would suggest the real cost ran higher than the low HR implied.
Watch the first easy runs back for elevated HR at normal pace, which would show the effort is still being paid down.
Watch when strength re-enters the log — its return marks that the trail block has been absorbed and normal rhythm resumed.
Watch whether sleep consolidates now that the crossing window has closed, since recent nights have been short and broken.

history.headline: The crossing is behind you and the first day off the trail is here. No run logged today — this is absorption, and that's the correct move. The story now is whether recovery signals come back cleanly.
watch_items: Watch whether the first easy runs back show elevated HR at normal pace, which would indicate the crossing is still being paid down.
Watch when strength re-enters the log — its return is the clearest marker that the block has been absorbed and normal rhythm has resumed.
Watch whether sleep consolidates now that the crossing window has closed, since the block's nights were short and broken.
Watch whether the calendar returns to its usual interleaved spread rather than staying sparse, as a prolonged gap would hint at a higher recovery cost than the low HR suggested.

history.headline: Second day off the trail, still no run logged. Absorption is taking longer than a single day — which is exactly right after three back-to-back ultra days. Watch for the first easy run to tell the real recovery story.
watch_items: Watch whether the first easy run back sits at normal HR for its pace, or runs elevated — the clearest read on whether the crossing is still being paid down.
Watch for strength to re-enter the log; its continued absence is now the most open thread from the block.
Watch whether the calendar returns to its usual interleaved rhythm rather than extending the current gap.
Watch whether sleep consolidates now that the block's short broken nights are behind you.
